title: Reminiscing the Way We Were in RCM
primary_topics: Speech at Rotary Club of Manila (RCM) reminiscing CJP's 1990-1991 RCM presidency, delivered November 16, 2023
The 'Love God Serve Man' credo -- how it was derived from Isaiah 42 and Mark 12:29-32 through Ignatian-style discernment, and why it was controversial in a civic club
The 1990 Luzon earthquake (7.7 Richter, 2,000+ deaths): RCM members pledged P7 million in response -- 16 times more than CJP's best expectation of P500,000

The story of how President-elect FVR offered CJP the Secretary of Justice portfolio, Leni objected, and FVR redirected him to the Supreme Court -- 'Under the saya ka pala. Dalawa na tayo. Sa Supreme Court ka na lang.'
sub_topics: RCM organized June 1, 1919 -- first and oldest Rotary Club in Asia, premier civic club in the Philippines

455 members during CJP's presidency -- largest in the world outside the US; counted Cabinet secretaries, senators, congressmen, justices, 40 doctors, 50 lawyers, bank presidents, ambassadors, executives of top 300 companies
RCM's unique election procedure: the Rotarian garnering the highest votes for Board membership is automatically proclaimed President -- no campaigning
18-month preparation leave from businesses, law office, and other activities for full-time RCM presidency
76-page Program of Action with 178 projects and P90 million budget -- 18 times the largest prior RCM budget of P5 million
Inaugural address July 12, 1990: 30-minute speech emphasizing Matthew 25 -- devoting resources to 'the least of our brothers'
Member reactions: from 'Why do you inject God in a civic club? This is divisive!' to 'Alleluia, what a spirit-filled speech!'
July 16, 1990 (4 days after inauguration): 7.7 Richter earthquake devastates Luzon -- 2,000+ deaths
July 19, 1990 (3 days after earthquake): CJP pleads for assistance; P5.5 million pledged in 30 minutes + P660,000 telephoned the next day; total of nearly P7 million (16x expectations)
Doctor medical missions; businessmen sent products; Rotary Anns sent clothes and groceries; CJP's relief team set up 250-family 'tent city' in Burnham Park, Baguio
Rotary Club of Waikiki: air-freighted over 3,300 kilos of relief goods from Hawaii in one shipment
Valedictory June 27, 1991: 185 projects implemented (7 more than planned, 95% completion); 72 committees formed
June 17, 1992: President-elect FVR called CJP for one-hour one-on-one meeting at Rm. 202, 845 Pasay Road, Makati -- offered Secretary of Justice post
CJP declined: 'I did not campaign for you. I voted for Salonga.' FVR: 'I know. But I want to be president of all our people... I know I can trust you to help me run the country.'

After two weeks, CJP declined citing Leni's objection: 'She did not have the gregarious talent expected from the wife of a political leader.' FVR: 'Ah, under the saya ka pala. Dalawa na tayo. Sa Supreme Court ka na lang.'
CJP's valedictory identity: 'the only Philippine Rotary President to become Chief Justice of the Philippines'

Isaiah 42 discernment: CJP and BLD community prayed over his presidency theme and were 'struck' by Isaiah 42:1-8 -- 'Here is my servant whom I uphold... I have called you for the victory of justice... a light for the nations... to open the eyes of the blind'

stances.claim: Attending Rotary meetings regularly is a life-changing civic act -- CJP's own Supreme Court appointment came directly from his friendship with Gen. Ramos as an RCM seatmate. The moral: 'Your seatmate may someday become the President of the Philippines and change forever the course of your life and career.'
stances.rhetorical_move: personal-testimony as proof-of-Rotary-concept: civic club membership as career-transforming network

stances.claim: 'Love God Serve Man' was not a divisive injection of religion into a civic club but a theological restatement of Paul Harris's own Rotary maxims -- 'Service above self. He profits most who serves best.' The credo merely names the theological root that was always already present.
stances.rhetorical_move: theological-reframing argument: God was always in Rotary; CJP merely named Him

stances.claim: The massive earthquake response (P7 million, 16 times expectations) was not merely a civic success but a divine affirmation -- the Lord's way of confirming the discernment and the 'Love God Serve Man' credo. Obedience to divine will produces disproportionate outpouring.
stances.rhetorical_move: providential-causation argument: divine amplification of human obedience

stances.claim: CJP went to the Supreme Court 'as a generous offer from one Rotarian to another' -- FVR's offer was not based on political loyalty (CJP voted for Salonga, not FVR) but on observed leadership competence: 'after observing how you succeeded in your RCM presidency, I know I can trust you to help me run the country.'
stances.rhetorical_move: performance-based-trust argument: civic leadership as the credential for national appointment
stances.confidence: asserted as direct quote from FVR

notable_anecdotes: The under-the-saya story: CJP told FVR he could not accept Secretary of Justice because 'my dear wife Leni objects -- she did not have the gregarious talent expected from the wife of a political leader.' FVR replied: 'Ah, under the saya ka pala. Dalawa na tayo. But you must serve our country. Sa Supreme Court ka na lang.'

The earthquake miracle: P5.5 million pledged in 30 minutes (+ P660,000 the next day) at one RCM meeting -- 16 times CJP's best expectation of P500,000. 'I thanked the Lord for this massive response... a sign of His Providence when we discern and obey His will.'
Tent city in Burnham Park, Baguio: CJP's relief team set up a tent city for 250 families after the 1990 Luzon earthquake.
Rotary Club of Waikiki: air-freighted over 3,300 kilos of relief goods from Hawaii in one shipment.

Isaiah 42 discernment: CJP and BLD members prayed over what his presidency theme should be; they were 'struck' by Isaiah 42:1-8 -- 'I have called you for the victory of justice... a light for the nations... to open the eyes of the blind.' 'I had goose bumps all over me. I could not believe that I could be the chosen one.'

The P90-million budget: 18 times the largest prior RCM budget of P5 million. Members were 'aghast.' CJP took comfort in Matthew 5:11-12: 'Blessed are you when they insult you... Be glad and rejoice, for your reward is great in heaven.'

FVR's RCM seatmate history: FVR was inducted in the same batch as CJP in 1983 -- then Chief of the Philippine Constabulary (later PNP); CJP would 'chitchat about the latest off-the-record events in our country.'
Valedictory: 185 projects implemented (7 more than the 178 planned), 95% completion, 72 committees, 94-page Final Report.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered November 16, 2023 at the Rotary Club of Manila, this speech by CJP responds to DGE Jackie Rodriguez's invitation to 'show our new members a wonderful glimpse of our glorious past' by reminiscing his 1990-1991 RCM presidency. He opens with a Shakespeare riff ('I come to bury Caesar, not to praise him -- but I have been subpoenaed to be buried instead') and jokes he intends to reach 100 ('only the good die young'). He first narrates how he got to the Supreme Court via a Rotary friendship: when he was inducted in 1983, his RCM seatmate was then-Philippine Constabulary chief Gen. Fidel V. Ramos; on June 17, 1992, FVR called CJP for a one-on-one meeting and offered him Secretary of Justice; CJP declined (he voted for Salonga, not FVR); FVR replied he wanted to 'be president of all our people' and cited CJP's RCM success as proof of trustworthiness; after CJP later cited Leni's objection, FVR uttered the famous line: 'Ah, under the saya ka pala. Dalawa na tayo. Sa Supreme Court ka na lang.' He then details his RCM presidency: 455-member club (largest in the world outside the US); his discernment with BLD members who were 'struck' by Isaiah 42 ('I have called you for the victory of justice... a light for the nations'); the 'Love God Serve Man' credo derived from Mark 12:29-32; a 76-page Program of Action with 178 projects and a P90-million budget (18 times the prior record of P5 million); member outcry and his Matthew 5:11-12 consolation ('Blessed are you when they insult you'). Four days after his July 12, 1990 inaugural, the 7.7-Richter Luzon earthquake struck (2,000+ deaths); three days later at an RCM meeting, CJP pleaded for assistance and members pledged P5.5 million in 30 minutes (plus P660,000 the next day), for a total of nearly P7 million -- 16 times his best expectation of P500,000. Relief operations included a 250-family tent city in Burnham Park, Baguio, and the Rotary Club of Waikiki air-freighting 3,300 kilos from Hawaii. His valedictory reported 185 projects implemented (7 more than planned), 95% completion, 72 committees, and a 94-page Final Report. He closes with the self-description as 'the only Philippine Rotary President to become Chief Justice of the Philippines' and with a sinner's prayer of surrender.
